newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO minister demands trial for Israeli officers.
newsitem.headline: PLO minister demands trial for Israeli officers.

text.p: A Palestinian cabinet minister called clashes in the West Bank on Wednesday a "planned crime" by the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and demanded Israel court-martial commanders who ordered troops to open fire.

Israeli soldiers near PLO-ruled Ramallah shot dead four Palestinians, wounded at least 200, and fought running gun battles with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's police in the bloodiest West Bank fighting since PLO rule began two years ago, witnesses and officials said.

Jamil al-Tarifi, minister of civil affairs who visited wounded in hospital, said: "We want to put on trial the Israeli officers who gave the order to open fire on Palestinians. Then we will talk with the Israeli government."
"I think it is a planned crime carried out by the Israeli government," Tarifi told Reuters. "We have said all along that our people will not be silent to Israeli crimes."
The clashes broke out as part of widespread protests in the West Bank and Gaza Strip against Netanyahu's decison to open a tunnel in Jerusalem near Islam's third holiest shrine.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers fired live ammunition and rubber bullets when they came under a hail of stones and bottles at a crossing to the Ramallah enclave, north of Jerusalem.

One angry Palestinian policeman grabbed a rifle and started shooting back at the Israelis, according to witnesses at the scene. Others from Arafat's Force 17 guard joined in, sparking the most serious gunfight between Israeli and Palestinian forces since Arafat returned to Gaza in July 1994.

The Israeli-PLO peace process has been virtually stalled since Netanyahu toppled Shimon Peres in May elections. Arafat said in Gaza on Wednesday the shootings had thrown relations with Netanyahu's right-wing government into crisis.
